Available filters: | **Filter** | **Type** | **Default** | **Description** | | - | - | - | - | | created_after | `String` | | Select contacts created after the given time (exclusive). ISO 8601 formatted string. The time to compare with is in UTC timezone | | updated_after | `String` | | Select contacts updated after the given time (exclusive). ISO 8601 formatted string. The time to compare with is in UTC timezone | | first_name | `String` | | Select contacts with the given first name. Case-insensitive | | last_name | `String` | | Select contacts with the given last name. Case-insensitive | | estimate_workflow_id | `Integer` | | Filters contacts by a single Estimate workflow | | invoice_workflow_id | `Integer` | | Filters contacts by a single Invoice workflow | | contact_type | `String` | | The contact type. Possible values `all`, `company`, `private_individual` | | delivery_method | `String` | | The delivery method for invoices. Possible values. Possible values `all`, `email`, `post`, `manual`, `peppol`, `simplerinvoicing` | | trusted_type | `String` | | Whether the contact is trusted. Possible values `all`, `trusted`, `not_trusted` | | mandate_type | `String` | | The direct debit mandate of the contact. api.description: Get general documents, one page at a time (scope: documents)

fields.description: Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `period:this_year,state:open`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: | **Filter** | **Type** | **Default** | **Description** | | - | - | - | - | | period | `String` | `this_year` | A named period (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom range (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years and must be between `20000101` and `21000101`. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. | | state | `String` | `all` | `all`, `new`, `saved`, `open`, `paid`, `late` or `pending_payment`. `paid`, `late` and `pending_payment` only apply to documents with a payment lifecycle (purchase invoices and receipts) | | recurring | `String` | `all` | `all`, `enabled` or `disabled` | | attachment | `String` | `all` | `all`, `with` or `without` | | reference | `String` | | Documents with the given reference value | | contact_id | `Integer` | | Documents belonging to the given contact | | ledger_account_id | `Integer` | | Documents booking against the given ledger account | | updated_after | `String` | | ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC; documents updated strictly after this time | Multiple values for `state`, `recurring` and `attachment` can be combined with a pipe, e.g. `state:open|paid`.
Sorts the list on date, so the newest (`date_desc`) or the oldest (`date_asc`) items come first.

fields.description: Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `period:this_year,state:open`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: | **Filter** | **Type** | **Default** | **Description** | | - | - | - | - | | period | `String` | `this_year` | A named period (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom range (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years and must be between `20000101` and `21000101`. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. | | state | `String` | `all` | `all`, `new`, `saved`, `open`, `paid`, `late` or `pending_payment`. `paid`, `late` and `pending_payment` only apply to documents with a payment lifecycle (purchase invoices and receipts) | | recurring | `String` | `all` | `all`, `enabled` or `disabled` | | attachment | `String` | `all` | `all`, `with` or `without` | | reference | `String` | | Documents with the given reference value | | contact_id | `Integer` | | Documents belonging to the given contact | | ledger_account_id | `Integer` | | Documents booking against the given ledger account | | updated_after | `String` | | ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC; documents updated strictly after this time | Multiple values for `state`, `recurring` and `attachment` can be combined with a pipe, e.g. `state:open|paid`.
Sorts the list on date, so the newest (`date_desc`) or the oldest (`date_asc`) items come first.

fields.description: Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `period:this_year,state:open`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: | **Filter** | **Type** | **Default** | **Description** | | - | - | - | - | | period | `String` | `this_year` | Matches on the document date. A named period (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom range (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years and must be between `20000101` and `21000101`. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. | | state | `String` | `all` | `all`, `new`, `saved`, `open`, `paid`, `late` or `pending_payment`. `paid`, `late` and `pending_payment` only apply to documents with a payment lifecycle (purchase invoices and receipts) | | recurring | `String` | `all` | `all`, `enabled` or `disabled` | | attachment | `String` | `all` | `all`, `with` or `without` | | automatic_saving | `String` | `all` | `all`, `automatic` or `manual`. `automatic` matches documents Moneybird saved by itself after analysing them; `manual` matches everything else, including documents nobody has saved yet | | reference | `String` | | Documents with the given reference value | | contact_id | `Integer` | | Documents belonging to the given contact | | ledger_account_id | `Integer` | | Documents booking against the given ledger account | | updated_after | `String` | | ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC; documents updated strictly after this time | The `period` filter matches on the document date. It does not look at the `period` of the individual details, which says which months the expenses belong to. Read `details[].period` in the response when you need those months, or use the reports endpoints, which already spread the amounts over that period. A detail's period can fall outside the filtered range, however wide you make it, so this filter cannot tell you which periods amounts fall in. Use the reports endpoints for that. Multiple values for `state`, `recurring` and `attachment` can be combined with a pipe, e.g. `state:open|paid`.
Sorts the list on date, so the newest (`date_desc`) or the oldest (`date_asc`) items come first.

fields.description: Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `period:this_year,state:open`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: | **Filter** | **Type** | **Default** | **Description** | | - | - | - | - | | period | `String` | `this_year` | Matches on the document date. A named period (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom range (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years and must be between `20000101` and `21000101`. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. | | state | `String` | `all` | `all`, `new`, `saved`, `open`, `paid`, `late` or `pending_payment`. `paid`, `late` and `pending_payment` only apply to documents with a payment lifecycle (purchase invoices and receipts) | | recurring | `String` | `all` | `all`, `enabled` or `disabled` | | attachment | `String` | `all` | `all`, `with` or `without` | | automatic_saving | `String` | `all` | `all`, `automatic` or `manual`. `automatic` matches documents Moneybird saved by itself after analysing them; `manual` matches everything else, including documents nobody has saved yet | | reference | `String` | | Documents with the given reference value | | contact_id | `Integer` | | Documents belonging to the given contact | | ledger_account_id | `Integer` | | Documents booking against the given ledger account | | updated_after | `String` | | ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC; documents updated strictly after this time | The `period` filter matches on the document date. It does not look at the `period` of the individual details, which says which months the expenses belong to. Read `details[].period` in the response when you need those months, or use the reports endpoints, which already spread the amounts over that period. A detail's period can fall outside the filtered range, however wide you make it, so this filter cannot tell you which periods amounts fall in. Use the reports endpoints for that. Multiple values for `state`, `recurring` and `attachment` can be combined with a pipe, e.g. `state:open|paid`.
Sorts the list on date, so the newest (`date_desc`) or the oldest (`date_asc`) items come first.

fields.description: Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `period:this_year,state:open`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: | **Filter** | **Type** | **Default** | **Description** | | - | - | - | - | | period | `String` | `this_year` | A named period (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom range (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years and must be between `20000101` and `21000101`. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. | | state | `String` | `all` | `all`, `new`, `saved`, `open`, `paid`, `late` or `pending_payment`. `paid`, `late` and `pending_payment` only apply to documents with a payment lifecycle (purchase invoices and receipts) | | recurring | `String` | `all` | `all`, `enabled` or `disabled` | | attachment | `String` | `all` | `all`, `with` or `without` | | reference | `String` | | Documents with the given reference value | | contact_id | `Integer` | | Documents belonging to the given contact | | ledger_account_id | `Integer` | | Documents booking against the given ledger account | | updated_after | `String` | | ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC; documents updated strictly after this time | Multiple values for `state`, `recurring` and `attachment` can be combined with a pipe, e.g. `state:open|paid`.
Sorts the list on date, so the newest (`date_desc`) or the oldest (`date_asc`) items come first.

fields.description: Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `period:this_year,state:all`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: | **Filter** | **Type** | **Default** | **Description** | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | state | `String` | `all` | `all`, `draft`, `open`, `late`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `billed` or `archived` | | period | `String` | `this_year` | Matches on the estimate date. This can either be the description of a period (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom period (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years and must be between `20000101` and `21000101`. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. | | contact_id | `Integer` | | Filters estimates by a single contact | | workflow_id | `Integer` | | Filters estimates by a single workflow | The `period` filter matches on the estimate date. It does not look at the `period` of the individual details, which says which months the expenses belong to. Read `details[].period` in the response when you need those months, or use the reports endpoints, which already spread the amounts over that period. A detail's period can fall outside the filtered range, however wide you make it, so this filter cannot tell you which periods amounts fall in. Use the reports endpoints for that. You can filter by multiple states at the same time as well. To do this, separate the state values by a pipe: `state:draft|scheduled`.

fields.description: Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `period:this_year,state:all`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: | **Filter** | **Type** | **Default** | **Description** | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | state | `String` | `all` | `all`, `new`, `open`, `late`, `paid`, or `uncollectible` | | period | `String` | `this_year` | Matches on the invoice date. This can either be the description of a period (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom period (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years and must be between `20000101` and `21000101`. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. | | contact_id | `Integer` | | Select invoices belonging to a certain contact | The `period` filter matches on the invoice date. It does not look at the `period` of the individual details, which says which months the expenses belong to. Read `details[].period` in the response when you need those months, or use the reports endpoints, which already spread the amounts over that period. A detail's period can fall outside the filtered range, however wide you make it, so this filter cannot tell you which periods amounts fall in. Use the reports endpoints for that. You can filter by multiple states at the same time as well. To do this, separate the state values by a pipe: `state:new|open`.

A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years and must be between `20000101` and `21000101`. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. | | contact_id | `Integer` | | Select invoices belonging to a certain contact | You can filter by multiple states at the same time as well. To do this, separate the state values by a pipe: `state:new|open`.

api.description: List sales invoices with a filter string such as 'state:open|paid' or 'period:this_year', one page at a time (scope: sales_invoices)

fields.description: Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `period:this_year,state:all`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: | **Filter** | **Type** | **Default** | **Description** | | - | - | - | - | | state | `String` | `all` | `all`, `draft`, `open`, `scheduled`, `pending_payment`, `late`, `reminded`, `paid` or `uncollectible` | | period | `String` | `this_year` | Matches on the invoice date. A period description (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom period (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. | | reference | `String` | | Select invoices with a certain reference | | contact_id | `Integer` | | Select invoices belonging to a certain contact | | recurring_sales_invoice_id | `Integer` | | Select invoices created by a certain recurring invoice | | workflow_id | `Integer` | | Select invoices that use a certain workflow | | created_after | `String` | | Select invoices created after the given time (exclusive). ISO 8601 formatted string. The time to compare with is in UTC timezone | | updated_after | `String` | | Select invoices updated after the given time (exclusive). ISO 8601 formatted string. The time to compare with is in UTC timezone | The `period` filter matches on the invoice date. It does not look at the `period` of the individual details, which says which months the expenses belong to. Read `details[].period` in the response when you need those months, or use the reports endpoints, which already spread the amounts over that period. A detail's period can fall outside the filtered range, however wide you make it, so this filter cannot tell you which periods amounts fall in. Use the reports endpoints for that. You can filter by multiple states at the same time by separating the values with a pipe (`state:draft|scheduled`). This also holds for the reference. A draft with no `invoice_date` set is only matched by a `period` when that period contains today. To list drafts irrespective of date, pass `state:draft` without a `period`; to narrow them down in time, use `created_after` or `updated_after`.
Sorts the list on date, so the newest (`date_desc`) or the oldest (`date_asc`) items come first.

api.description: List all available tax rates for the administration, one page at a time (scopes: any of settings, sales_invoices, documents or estimates)

fields.description: Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `percentage:21,tax_rate_type:sales_invoice`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: | **Filter** | **Type** | **Default** | **Description** | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | name | `String` | | Select tax rates by their full name | | partial_name | `String` | | Select tax rates with this substring in their name | | percentage | `Integer` | | Select tax rates with the specified percentage, e.g. specify `21` for 21% | | tax_rate_type | `String` | | `general_journal_document`, `purchase_invoice` or `sales_invoice`. Without this filter, tax rates of all types are returned | | country | `String` | | Select tax rates with the specified country. Must be a 2 letter abbreviation following ISO 3166. Please note that only foreign tax rates will have this field set. Domestic tax rates will not have this set at the moment. | | show_tax | `Boolean` | | Use `true` to tax rates for which tax is shown on the invoice, `false` for when it's not shown. No value will select both | | active | `Boolean` | | Use `true` to select active tax rates. Use `false` for inactive tax rates. No value will select both | | created_after | `String` | | Tax rates created after the given time (exclusive). ISO 8601 formatted string. The time to compare with is in UTC timezone | | updated_after | `String` | | Tax rates updated after the given time (exclusive). ISO 8601 formatted string. The time to compare with is in UTC timezone | You can filter by multiple tax rate types at the same time by separating the values with a pipe (`tax_rate_type:purchase_invoice|sales_invoice`).

api.description: List all time entries, one page at a time (scope: time_entries)

fields.description: Filters are `key:value` terms separated by commas (e.g. `period:this_year,state:all`). Any filter you pass replaces the defaults below entirely, so include every key you need. Available filters: | **Filter** | **Type** | **Default** | **Description** | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | state | `String` | `all` | `all`, `open` or `non_billable` | | period | `String` | `this_year` | This can either be the description of a period (`this_week`, `prev_week`, `next_week`, `this_month`, `prev_month`, `next_month`, `this_quarter`, `prev_quarter`, `next_quarter`, `this_year`, `prev_year`, `next_year`) or a custom period (`201301..201302`, `20130101..20130131`). A custom period must have a start and an end date. It must not be longer than 10 years and must be between `20000101` and `21000101`. For one month, use `202401..202401`, not `202401`. Without `period`, the filter does not limit the dates. The default `this_year` applies only when you send no `filter`. | | contact_id | `Integer` | | Select time entries belonging to a certain contact | | include_nil_contacts | `Boolean` | false | Whether to include time entries that have no assigned contact | | include_active | `Boolean` | false | Whether to include active time entries i.e. time entries without ended_at | | project_id | `Integer` | | Select time entries belonging to a certain project | | user_id | `Integer` | | Select time entries belonging to a certain user | | day | `Date` | | Select time entries on a specific date | You can filter by multiple states at the same time as well. To do this, separate the state values by a pipe: `state:open|non_billable`.
Free-text search across the time entry description.
